authorization: Researcher prioritizes decoding phase transitions and correction thresholds in the continuing Lab 008 study.
question: Does the selector-compatible diamond fan survive an exact square-strip embedding with the physical full-charge majority law strongly enough to make kappa diverge?
claim_boundary: The isolated diamond template is only a compatibility witness. This contract tests the missing embedding and physical-probability factors on bounded-width strips; it cannot establish the two-dimensional square threshold.
alternatives: Derive a transfer recurrence for target multiplicity, majority-domain membership and full charge on the width-three square strip.
Compute exact exponential rates of majority-domain mass and selector second moment for the embedded fan family.
Prove that outside earlier paths or the charge-majority filter destroys the isolated ladder, closing this obstruction route.
planned_steps: Validate the strip transfer against direct enumeration for one through four diamonds using the frozen shortest-then-lexicographic selector.
Propagate exact integer counts only while the frontier state stays within the registered cap; record numerator and denominator rates separately.
Stop at a proved fixed-width growth/decay rate, a destroyed embedding, or a named transfer-state obstruction.
acceptance_criteria: Direct n<=4 controls reproduce the registered isolated-template histogram before any transfer extrapolation.
The embedded model states all added square edges, measured charges, rough boundaries, logical cut and selector order.
Any obstruction reports the exact physical majority-domain denominator together with the selector second moment.
Fixed-width evidence is not promoted to a two-dimensional midpoint or threshold claim.
stop_rule: Do not enumerate a canonical L5 square, fit finite sizes, or infer a 2D threshold. Stop after the bounded width-three transfer/embedding matrix.
decision: The physical width-three square-strip embedding retains finite fan multiplicity at W=4 (A=3926, selector second moment 7968, kappa=3984/1963, maximum multiplicity five). Exact charge-majority transfer reaches W=5, then fails closed at the registered state cap during W=6. The nonlocal selector moment still requires a reduced availability automaton; no fixed-width rate, midpoint classification or threshold follows.
